texts.label: A
texts.title: The planner
texts.text: Urban trees are infrastructure. They lower summer temperatures and interrupt rainwater as effectively as some engineered systems. Treating them as decoration makes their maintenance seem optional, when in fact it is part of managing a city. Calling trees infrastructure also makes failure measurable. A dead planting is a maintenance decision that should be reviewed before another scheme is announced. The disagreement is about distribution as well as ecology, since a successful intervention must be maintained and shared by the people who live with its consequences. The strongest position is not the loudest one; it is the account that recognises what its preferred solution leaves unresolved and explains how visitors, residents or colleagues might respond. This qualification keeps comparison meaningful: each writer offers a preference, but also identifies a cost that a less careful account might ignore.

texts.label: B
texts.title: The ecologist
texts.text: The strongest case for trees is not their convenience to humans. A street can support insects, birds and fungi if planting is diverse and connected. The ecological benefits are easily lost when every tree is selected for appearance alone. Diversity concerns soil, continuity and the ability of different organisms to use the same corridor at different times of year. The disagreement is about distribution as well as ecology, since a successful intervention must be maintained and shared by the people who live with its consequences. The strongest position is not the loudest one; it is the account that recognises what its preferred solution leaves unresolved and explains how visitors, residents or colleagues might respond. This qualification keeps comparison meaningful: each writer offers a preference, but also identifies a cost that a less careful account might ignore.

texts.label: C
texts.title: The resident
texts.text: I support more trees, but I dislike schemes that ignore the people who live beside them. Roots can damage pavements and dense shade can make a narrow street feel unsafe. Consultation should shape planting rather than follow it. Consultation is most useful before the planting plan becomes expensive to alter. Residents know where shade, roots or visibility will matter. The disagreement is about distribution as well as ecology, since a successful intervention must be maintained and shared by the people who live with its consequences. The strongest position is not the loudest one; it is the account that recognises what its preferred solution leaves unresolved and explains how visitors, residents or colleagues might respond. This qualification keeps comparison meaningful: each writer offers a preference, but also identifies a cost that a less careful account might ignore.

texts.label: D
texts.title: The economist
texts.text: The benefits of trees are real, though difficult to distribute evenly. A new park may raise nearby property values and push out the residents it was intended to help. Greening policy therefore needs measures that protect affordability. Equity changes the definition of success. A city can increase canopy while distributing comfort, risk and rising rents unequally. The disagreement is about distribution as well as ecology, since a successful intervention must be maintained and shared by the people who live with its consequences. The strongest position is not the loudest one; it is the account that recognises what its preferred solution leaves unresolved and explains how visitors, residents or colleagues might respond. This qualification keeps comparison meaningful: each writer offers a preference, but also identifies a cost that a less careful account might ignore.

questions.prompt: Who argues that trees should be managed as a fundamental city service?
questions.explanation: The planner calls trees infrastructure and links them to city management.

questions.prompt: Who is most concerned with species variety?
questions.explanation: The ecologist recommends diverse and connected planting for wildlife.

questions.prompt: Who insists that local people should influence decisions?
questions.explanation: The resident says consultation should shape planting.

questions.prompt: Who warns that an environmental improvement can have an unintended social cost?
questions.explanation: The economist links parks with rising property values and displacement.
